author: world today news
title: DeSantis Declares Tate Brothers 'Not Welcome' in Florida After Romania Exit
text:
• Florida Governor Ron DeSantis stated that Andrew and Tristan Tate are not welcome in Florida.
• The Tate brothers are facing serious charges in Romania, including human trafficking and sexual intercourse with a minor.
• They arrived at Fort Lauderdale Executive Airport after a travel ban from Romanian authorities was lifted.
• DeSantis learned about their arrival through the media and emphasized Florida's limited power to prevent their visit.
• Florida's Attorney General, James Uthmeier, is exploring legal options regarding the Tates' presence in the state.
• Uthmeier has initiated a preliminary inquiry into the Tate brothers, focusing on human trafficking and violence against women.
• Andrew Tate asserted their innocence upon arrival, claiming they have no criminal record.
• The Tate brothers' attorney criticized DeSantis's remarks, stating they are American citizens and victims of defamation.
• The Tates plan to return to Romania at the end of March to meet with prosecutors.
• Former President Donald Trump stated he knows nothing about the Tates' arrival and will check into the matter.
• U.K. Prime Minister Keir Starmer acknowledged human trafficking as a security risk and pledged to investigate.
• Matthew Jury, representing alleged victims, expressed dismay at the Tates' arrival in the U.S.
• The Tates are under criminal examination in Romania for forming an organized criminal group and other charges.
• Romania's DIICOT confirmed that judicial control measures remain in place despite the Tates' departure.
• The situation has sparked discussions about the complexities of international law enforcement regarding human trafficking.
